concepts.name: Living Form
concepts.axis: Spacious sculptural product stage; cream and terracotta
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE exceptionally CLEAN, eye-catching desktop homepage IMAGE for ALKEBULAN, a modern African streetwear brand. Landscape 1536 x 1024, front-on finished website, no laptop/device frame or montage of screens. The user rejected the previous designs for being cluttered and wants the original spacious Living Canvas sophistication combined with African contemporary art and streetwear. Apply serious community UI-design principles: ONE dominant visual composition, precise alignment, generous margins, no more than TWO typefaces, ONE accent color, one primary shop action, clear product hierarchy. At least 40 percent of the hero must be genuinely CALM negative space. Impress through scale, crop, shape, material and typography, not visual quantity. A beautiful real-looking fashion image or the actual product should carry the visual weight.
Clean polished contemporary design. NO grunge, distressed fonts, ink speckles, scratches, noise overlays, repeated mask wallpaper, tiled faces, crowded murals, chaotic collages, stickers, busy borders, badges, fake stats or ornamental card grids. NEVER put background graphics behind small text. Text stays readable and never crosses a model's face or the garment print. No aggressive 200px headlines crowding the navigation. This should feel like a meticulously art-directed modern fashion website, not a festival flyer.
African identity comes from the actual Ijele, Durbar or Dùn Dùn print, contemporary Black fashion representation where requested, and ONE restrained original modern-art gesture. Cultural marks are creative contemporary art, not fabricated sacred writing or claimed historical artifacts. No safari tropes or ceremonial costumes. Clothing styling is contemporary oversized tees, wide-leg trousers, understated jewelry.
Preserve each supplied garment's original black fabric, visible print, lettering, colors and proportions. Model clothing must retain the same graphic. Do not invent products. No fabricated price, discount, stock status, reviews or partner logos. Correct wordmark ALKEBULAN. Refined small navigation 'Collection  Men  Women  Our story', simple thin search and bag symbols. One clear 'Shop the collection' button. Use short copy. Avoid duplicate slogans. Show the beginning of one calm next section at the bottom, without filling the entire lower screen with three tiny product cards. Optional discreet concept number/name must be small and outside the navigation.

Reference roles: 1 is the owner's selected spacious Living Canvas homepage, for clean spacing, rounded forms and sophisticated typography only. 2 is the REAL Ijele product to preserve. 3 is a contemporary graphic-face reference for FORM ONLY: extract the strength of a SINGLE abstract eye/nose/profile; do not repeat faces or copy its distressed texture.
CONCEPT 01 / LIVING FORM. Warm chalk-white canvas, near-black typography, ONE burnt terracotta accent. A thin ivory capsule navigation floats 32px from the top with generous side margins and ALKEBULAN at left. Hero is an exceptionally spacious asymmetric composition: on the RIGHT half, the actual Ijele tee is crisply isolated and floats in front of ONE large smooth terracotta circular bas-relief. Within the disk, a beautifully designed abstract contemporary African portrait is expressed through just a bold half-eye, a curved nose, and three sculpted braid-like grooves, modern sculpture and flat graphic design meeting in one piece. Soft dimensional highlights, no room/arch/interior scene, no archaeological artifact. The disk and shirt form ONE coherent object group occupying 43% of page width, with plenty of clear cream around it. LEFT side has a masterful typographic composition: large clean condensed 'CULTURE' with smaller refined italic 'in motion.' below, carrying the sophistication of the selected screenshot. One short sentence 'African roots. Unrestricted expression.' followed by a restrained dark capsule shop button. Vast calm space above and below the copy. Tiny product caption 'Ijele / Wearable artwork' tucked under the tee, no floating stacked cards. A thin understated three-name text selector can sit below the focal object, without bubbles. The bottom 12% begins an ivory editorial section with simple heading 'The wearable archive' and one partial garment crop. Polished clean material, photographic cotton detail, disciplined beautiful spacing. The overall feel is African art in a forward-looking streetwear store, NOT a decor brand.

CONCEPT 03 / COBALT RHYTHM. A startlingly fresh clean African graphic-art streetwear site. Color system CHALK WHITE, rich COBALT BLUE and dark ink. Crisp white navigation at top, ALKEBULAN in bold dark condensed lettering on left and small orderly links on right. Hero uses a vast white field with an intentional asymmetric composition. LEFT: beautifully spaced headline 'Wear your' in black contemporary geometric sans and the word 'rhythm.' in a custom rounded cobalt display style; generous text size but only two lines, with wide open margins. Small copy 'African expression. Everyday form.' Single cobalt rounded shop button. RIGHT: ONE enormous cobalt smooth paper-cut SCULPTURE of a contemporary abstract face, built from a single oversized eye, cheek curve and short vertical braid-like ribs. An elegant graphic object, not a historical mask, and not a collage. The sculpture creates a crisp blue vertical silhouette, partially cropped by the right edge, taking at most 35% of hero width; real soft light and shallow layered shadows make it tactile. The original Dùn Dùn tee floats in front and slightly left of the blue artwork at an unusually clear, generous scale, front print intact. Leave clean white gaps around all object contours; no mark behind copy, no extra zigzags, no dots, no badge. An understated Dùn Dùn caption and two thin arrow controls sit near the garment's lower edge. At the bottom starts a restrained blue band with very small white 'Ijele / Durbar / Dùn Dùn' and one quietly cropped fashion detail. Personality: a contemporary African design studio's premium streetwear store, playful through one exceptional form and excellent type, not through a barrage of graphics.
